In one sentence: the analysis recommends **buying a managed identity provider** (e.g. WorkOS, Clerk, or Auth0) as the authentication engine — sessions, credential storage, password reset, MFA, and SSO turned on only when actually needed — while building only a thin, product-owned layer for tenant/role modeling and audit display, rather than rolling sessions/crypto/MFA by hand on a 7-person team with no security engineer under deadline pressure; overall confidence is **LOW**, not because the direction is in doubt (every chain's uncertainty would, if resolved, sharpen rather than reverse the recommendation) but because two of the three supporting chains each carry two unresolved axes of uncertainty (an unnamed/unaudited OSS library, an unverified 12–24 month enterprise-SSO timeline, and an unpriced estimate-calibration assumption).
